name: EMC2301-1-ACZL-TR
title: EMC2301/2/3/5: SMBus fan controllers, one to five RPM-based PWM channels
summary: A family of SMBus fan controllers for 4-wire fans, with one (EMC2301), two (EMC2302), three (EMC2303) or five (EMC2305) PWM outputs, each paired with a tachometer input. Every channel runs either in direct duty mode or under a closed-loop PID algorithm that holds a target tach count, with spin-up, ramp-rate limiting, stall and aging-fan detection, and an ALERT output. A watchdog drives every fan to full speed when the host goes quiet for 4 s. EMC2301-1-ACZL-TR is the one-channel part in MSOP-8 at fixed address 0101_111, on tape and reel.
key_figures: ±1% max with 32.768 kHz external clock, ±2% max internal

operation.topic: Two ways to drive each fan
operation.text: Each channel works in one of two modes. In Direct Setting mode the host writes a duty value to the Fan Setting register and the output follows at once (Equation 4-1); ramp-rate limiting is available through ENRCx. In Fan Speed Control (FSC) mode, enabled by ENAGx, the host writes a target tachometer count and a PID loop adjusts the duty to reach it, with spin-up and ramp control. Entering Direct Setting mode restores the last value written to Fan Setting.

Each output is open drain by default and can be made push-pull, with normal or inverted polarity. Its frequency is one of four base frequencies (26.00 kHz, 19.531 kHz, 4.882 kHz, 2.441 kHz) divided by the 8-bit PWM Divide register, which reaches about 9.5 Hz from the 2.441 kHz base. Divide values 00h and 01h both mean 1. Duty has 256 steps.

The loop uses proportional, integral and derivative terms, and its accuracy follows the accuracy of the clock. The target is the number of 32.768 kHz periods in one fan revolution; for a 2-pole fan at 3000 RPM that is 1296 (51h in the TACH Target register). A target of FFh turns the fan off for lower supply current. The loop is off after power-up. Its defaults suit many fans, so writing the TACH Target alone sets a speed; the loop works with fans up to 16000 RPM that give a valid tach signal.

Optional steps first, if the defaults do not suit: spin-up level and time; fan step size; minimum drive that keeps the fan turning; update time and edge count; the Valid TACH Count, as the highest count that still means the fan is turning. Then write the TACH Target and set ENAGx. Microchip application note AN17.4 tabulates RPM against tach counts for the 500, 1k, 2k and 4k ranges.

An error window of 0, 50, 100 or 200 RPM around the target stops the loop adjusting the drive once the speed is close enough, which avoids hunting (motor-boating) with awkward fans. The loop still computes corrections inside the window but does not apply them.
DPTx picks the derivative form (none, basic, step, both). The Gain register scales KP, KI and KD by 1x, 2x, 4x (default) or 8x each.

The Max Step register (1 to 31 counts) and the update time (100 ms to 1.6 s) limit how fast the drive changes: when a new setting differs from the present one by more than the step, the drive moves one step per update period until it arrives. Under FSC ramp control is always on; in Direct Setting mode it is on when ENRCx is set. With the FSC defaults of Fan Configuration 2, the maximum step is not applied.

Under FSC the drive never falls below the Fan Minimum Drive value unless the target is FFh. Should the fan halt for whatever cause, low drive included, the loop tries to restart it; a minimum drive that keeps the fan running avoids oscillation between stalling and restarting.

The TACHx input is timed continuously: the reading is the number of clock periods across the chosen number of edges (3, 5, 7 or 9), shown as a count proportional to the revolution period. With five edges on a 2-pole fan and the 32.768 kHz clock, the count is the clock periods per revolution. The measurement runs in either mode, so in Direct Setting mode it serves as a diagnostic; a drive too low for the fan, zero included, can then report a stall and raise an interrupt. Measuring more edges than the fan's poles give scales the reported speed by the effective multiplier, and the target must be adjusted to match; Microchip gives settings for fans with other than two poles on request.

A reading above the Valid TACH Count means a stalled fan: the stall bit is set, an interrupt raised and, under FSC, the loop runs spin-up again and keeps retrying until the fan turns or the loop is disabled. A target above the Valid TACH Count is ignored and the present drive kept. In Direct Setting mode, and during spin-up, the stall interrupt is masked for the programmed spin-up time; in Direct Setting mode the stall bit is otherwise set whenever the reading passes the Valid count. Under FSC the check happens at each update, not continuously.

With the drive at full scale, if the measured speed stays short of the target by more than the Drive Fail Band for 16, 32 or 64 update periods (DFCx), the DRVFx bit is set and ALERT asserted. This flags a fan whose top speed has dropped with age or a target faster than the fan can turn. It is used only while FSC is active; it is off by default.

Spin-up starts in Direct Setting mode when the setting goes from 00h to any other value, and under FSC when the target changes from FFh to a value below the Valid TACH Count or when the reading rises above the Valid TACH Count. The output goes to 100% for the first quarter of the spin-up time (unless NKCKx skips this kick), then holds the spin level (30% to 65%) for the rest. At the end the tach is checked: a reading still above the Valid TACH Count sets FNSPIN and the routine retries.

Tach timing uses either an external 32.768 kHz clock driven into CLK or the internal 32 kHz oscillator; accuracy follows the clock's. With DRECK set, CLK drives the internal clock out push-pull so other controllers can share it. What CLK does at power-up does not depend on how it is configured afterwards. The added CLK roles are on EMC2303/5 only.

operation.topic: Address and default speed by pull-up (EMC2303/5)
operation.text: At power-up ADDR_SEL reads one of six pull-up values to choose the SMBus address. With 33 k on ADDR_SEL, the pull-up on CLK selects the default drive of every fan (0, 30, 50, 75 or 100%), and CLK then carries only that pull-up to VDD and is not otherwise used. A non-zero default drive is applied without spin-up, and the watchdog keeps working.

If 4 s pass without SMBus activity, the watchdog sets WATCH, drives every fan to full scale until it is reprogrammed, asserts ALERT and turns FSC off; turning the watchdog off afterwards neither restores the drive nor re-enables FSC. In power-up mode it runs once from power-on and stops for good when it fires or when the host writes a Fan Setting register or sets ENAGx; other register writes do not stop it, and no stall check runs while it is active. With WD_EN set it runs continuously, restarting after every access to the register set.

SMBus 2.0 client with Write Byte, Read Byte, Send Byte, Receive Byte and Block Read/Write (Block transfers in I2C format only), with the register pointer auto-incrementing and wrapping from FFh to 00h. The device accepts clock stretching but never stretches the clock. EMC2301 answers at 0101_111. A time-out resets the interface after 30 ms of inactivity; it is off by default (DIS_TO set) and enabled by clearing DIS_TO. The interface also resets when both lines stay high for more than 150 µs. When ALERT is asserted the device answers the Alert Response Address 0001_100 with its own address and, once the address has gone out whole, sets MASK to release ALERT.

Defaults load at power-on reset when VDD rises past the POR level. Reading a high byte copies the matching low byte to a shadow register so the pair is consistent; a later read of the high byte refreshes it. Status bits clear when read once the fault has gone. Setting LOCK makes all SWL registers read-only until power is cycled.

MSOP parts carry two customer-specific lines on the front (2301 or 2302 with a code) and year, week and traceability codes on the back; QFN parts carry the part number with a year-week-traceability line. e3 marks matte tin, Pb-free.
